newsitem.title: USA: NY Times endorses Torricelli in New Jersey race.
newsitem.headline: NY Times endorses Torricelli in New Jersey race.

text.p: The New York Times on Monday gave a tepid endorsement to Democratic Representative Robert Torricelli for U.S. Senate in New Jersey, praising his record on social services but voicing doubts over his conduct in office.
Torricelli is running against Republican Representative Richard Zimmer to fill the seat being vacated by retiring Democratic Sen. Bill Bradley. Polls show the two running neck-to-neck.
Both candidates "come across as scorched-earth partisans who have brought no honour to New Jersey this year," the newspaper wrote, calling its decision "a close and not particularly pleasant one."

While Zimmer is a moderate Republican, his votes in Congress on environmental funding and guns and his support for budget-cutting measures backed by House Speaker Newt Gingrich cost him the Times' support, it wrote.

It noted Torriceli's voting record in Congress "on preserving social services, health and education programmes." It also lauded him for what it called a "courageous" decision to back President Clinton's deficit-reduction package in 1993 and his move to accuse the Central Intelligence Agency of backing violence in Guatemala.
But it pointed out that he had a reputation as a maverick, adding, "We are not timid about listing our reservations about his conduct of this campaign and his Congressional career."

Torricelli's "fundraising among special interests has also been troubling," it said. "So has his casual concern about the proprieties of office," it said, referring to his taking custody of a girl whose father fled the country while under indictment.
